blocks.text: On Monday evening, the courtyard of a home at Dhekaha in ward 1 of Pipara Rural Municipality, Mahottari, was crowded with neighbours. A pall of grief hung over the gathering. Sitting quietly and struggling to steady herself was 41-year-old Indrika Devi Mahato. Her husband Bharat Mahato, 45, who had been working as a labourer in Saudi Arabia, was killed in a drone attack on October 21. The strike was part of an escalating series of attacks launched by Iran-backed Houthi rebels targeting locations in Saudi Arabia—a tragic blow for an impoverished Nepali family entirely unconnected to the conflict.
